Glossary

Every term, defined in one place.

Term Definition
Codepoint The atomic unit of SuperUnicode; a 31-bit SUCS_CP value in Base, or a 64-bit sucs_ex_char_t in Extended.
Block A named run of codepoints, recorded in Blocks.txt.
Range A declared contiguous allocation, e.g. a plugin’s codepoint range.
Plane 64,536 codepoints; plane = CP >> 16.
District 16 planes (1 MiB); district = CP >> 20.
Zone 16 districts (16 MiB); zone = CP >> 24.
Territory 16 zones (256 MiB); territory = CP >> 28.
Unicode Compatibility Space 0x000000–0x10FFFF, permanently 1:1 with Unicode.
System Control Plane (SCP) 0x110000–0x11FFFF; machine instructions, host of the BANcode Registry.
BANcode Registry The BANcode, WARNcode, COMcode and SOFTcode diagnostic blocks.
Trap 0x7FFFFFF0–0x7FFFFFFE; raises the stream into diagnostics.
Sentinel 0x7FFFFFFF; end-of-stream marker, never an allocation.
SUCD The SuperUnicode machine-instruction database, versioned under /Public.
SUTR A SuperUnicode Technical Report (SUTR-0 through SUTR-6).
ExtSUCS SuperUnicode Extended; the unbounded 64-bit space above the Base ceiling.
Base limit 0x7FFFFFFF; the default runtime ceiling and the floor for plugin ranges.
Plugin A package of codepoints above the base limit, mounted after the checksum gate.
Checksum gate CRC32c + Fletcher-64 verification of a plugin blob at boot.
OWFS The OpenWindows native drive filesystem (libowfs.a).
USFS The portable external-media filesystem (libusfs.a).
SUTF SUCS UTF-8/16/32 framing — the endian-neutral codepoint ↔ word-sequence transformations (see SUTF framing).
SUST SuperUnicode Serialization Transports — the byte-packing layer: SUST-16 (SUTF-16 words in explicit big-endian canonical or little-endian order, no surrogates), SUST-32/64/128/256/512/N fixed-width, and e-SUST page-mapped IPC (modules/sust).
SUCA The SuperUnicode Collation Algorithm.
SGW The System Glyph Width & Monospace Grid standard — East_Asian_Width-style width classification and the O(1) fixed-cell grid metric.
SBR The System Boundary & Line Break Rules standard — single-pass deterministic line breaking (a UAX #14 analog) over the full 64-bit SUCS space, with explicit SCP break markers.
SUCF SuperUnicode Canonical Forms — the dual-target canonical (de)composition engine (a UAX #15 analog): SUCF-C composes for compact storage/equality, SUCF-D decomposes for analysis/sorting; zero allocation over the 64-bit space (see SUCF canonical forms).
Cursor Position in the instruction stream; printable codepoints advance it, control codepoints do not.
